title: AMC 8 — Mock Test 01 (Variant Edition)
instructions: 25 questions · 40 minutes · No calculator. 1 point per correct answer, no penalty for wrong answers.

questions.question: What is the value of this expression in decimal form? $$\frac{55}{11}+\frac{110}{55}+\frac{55}{1100}$$
Four squares with side lengths $2, 5, 6,$ and $9$ are placed side by side in a row so that adjacent squares touch. What is the total width of the row?
questions.solution: The widths add up: $2+5+6+9=22$.

questions.question: When Keisha added all the integers from $1$ to $10$, she accidentally left out one number. Her incorrect sum was a perfect square. Which number did she leave out?
questions.solution: $1+2+\cdots+10=55$. The only perfect square reachable by removing one number from $1$–$10$ is $49=55-6$. She left out $6$.

questions.question: Mateo rolls two standard 6-sided dice. What is the probability that the product of the two numbers rolled is a multiple of $4$?

In a race, runner $A$ finished ahead of runner $B$, runner $B$ finished ahead of runner $C$, and runner $D$ finished ahead of runner $A$. Which of the following could be the order in which they finished?
questions.solution: The conditions force $D$ before $A$, $A$ before $B$, and $B$ before $C$: the only possible order is $D,A,B,C$.

questions.question: A $2\times 5$ rectangle must be completely covered by $1\times 2$ dominoes (which may be rotated). In how many different ways can this be done?
questions.solution: Let $T(n)$ be the number of domino tilings of a $2\times n$ board. The right end is either a vertical domino ($T(n-1)$ ways) or two horizontal dominoes ($T(n-2)$ ways), so $T(n)=T(n-1)+T(n-2)$ with $T(1)=1$, $T(2)=2$: $1,2,3,5,8$. Thus $T(5)=8$.

questions.question: On Monday, Diego has $\$1$. Every day, he either gains $\$2$ or doubles the amount of money he had the previous day. How many different amounts of money could he have after exactly $3$ days?

All the beads in Ana's jar are red, blue, or green. She has twice as many red beads as blue beads, and $3$ more green beads than red beads. She has $28$ beads in all. How many green beads does she have?
questions.solution: Let blue $=x$; then red $=2x$ and green $=2x+3$. So $x+2x+(2x+3)=28$, giving $5x=25$, $x=5$, and green $=2(5)+3=13$.

questions.question: In $1985$ a weather station recorded a carbon dioxide level of $340$ ppm. The level increased by exactly $2$ ppm every year. What was the level in $2030$?
questions.solution: $2030-1985=45$ years, so the level is $340+45\cdot 2=430$ ppm.

questions.question: The vertices of $\triangle ABC$ are $A(2,3)$, $B(8,3)$, and $C(5,y)$ with $y>3$. The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $15$. What is $y$?
questions.solution: $AB$ is horizontal with length $8-2=6$. From $\tfrac12\cdot 6\cdot h=15$ the height is $h=5$, so $y=3+5=8$.

questions.question: Rosa keeps $66$ fish in $4$ tanks. There is $1$ more fish in the 2nd tank than in the 1st, $2$ more in the 3rd than in the 2nd, and $3$ more in the 4th than in the 3rd. How many fish are in the 4th tank?
questions.solution: The tanks hold $t,\ t+1,\ t+3,\ t+6$ fish. Then $4t+10=66$, so $t=14$, and the 4th tank has $14+6=20$ fish.

questions.question: A bunny hops up a staircase of $4$ steps, going up either $1$ step or $2$ steps at a time. In how many different ways can the bunny reach the top?

One-way roads connect towns as follows: $A\to B$ is $3$ km, $B\to C$ is $4$ km, $A\to C$ is $9$ km, $C\to D$ is $2$ km, and $B\to D$ is $8$ km. What is the length in km of the shortest route from $A$ to $D$?
questions.solution: Compare the routes: $A\to B\to C\to D=3+4+2=9$; $A\to C\to D=9+2=11$; $A\to B\to D=3+8=11$. The shortest is $9$ km.

questions.question: Let $A$ and $B$ be distinct nonzero digits such that the two-digit number $\underline{A}\,\underline{B}$ minus the two-digit number $\underline{B}\,\underline{A}$ equals $45$. How many such two-digit numbers $\underline{A}\,\underline{B}$ are there?
questions.solution: $\underline{A}\,\underline{B}-\underline{B}\,\underline{A}=9(A-B)=45$, so $A-B=5$. With $B\ge 1$: $(A,B)=(6,1),(7,2),(8,3),(9,4)$ — $4$ numbers.

questions.question: Zoe writes each of the integers from $1$ to $25$ into the cells of a $5\times 5$ grid, one number per cell, and computes the product of the numbers in each row. What is the greatest possible number of rows whose product is odd?
questions.solution: A row product is odd only if every cell in it is odd. There are $13$ odd numbers among $1$–$25$, and each all-odd row needs $5$, so at most $\lfloor 13/5\rfloor=2$ rows can work — and $2$ is achievable.

questions.question: A chess king attacks every square one step away horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. In how many ways can two identical kings be placed on two different squares of a $2\times 3$ board so that they do not attack each other?
questions.solution: There are $\binom{6}{2}=15$ pairs of squares. Attacking pairs: $8$ across adjacent columns (2 horizontal + 2 diagonal per column pair, times 2 column pairs) plus $3$ vertical pairs, $11$ total. Non-attacking: $15-11=4$.

questions.question: Three concentric circles have radii $2$, $3$, and $4$. The area of the ring between the circles of radius $2$ and radius $3$ is what fraction of the area of the largest circle?
questions.solution: Ring area $=\pi(3^2-2^2)=5\pi$; largest circle area $=16\pi$. The fraction is $\frac{5\pi}{16\pi}=\frac{5}{16}$.

questions.question: In a class, $\frac{3}{4}$ of the students like math and $\frac{2}{3}$ like science. Every student likes at least one of the two subjects. What fraction of the class likes both subjects?
questions.solution: Inclusion–exclusion: $\frac34+\frac23-\text{both}=1$, so $\text{both}=\frac{9}{12}+\frac{8}{12}-\frac{12}{12}=\frac{5}{12}$.

questions.question: How many triangles can be formed by choosing any three vertices of a regular hexagon?
questions.solution: No three vertices of a regular hexagon are collinear, so any 3 vertices form a triangle: $\binom{6}{3}=20$.

questions.question: An army of $12$ frogs sits in a tree. Frogs in the shade are green and frogs in the sun are yellow. Right now there are $4$ more green frogs than yellow frogs. How many green frogs are there?
questions.solution: Let yellow $=y$; then green $=y+4$ and $2y+4=12$, so $y=4$ and green $=8$.

questions.question: A roll of tape has an outer diameter of $6$ inches and is wound around a ring of diameter $2$ inches, so a cross section is an annulus. If the tape is $0.01$ inches thick, how many inches long is the tape? (The length equals the annulus area divided by the thickness.)
questions.solution: Annulus area $=\pi(3^2-1^2)=8\pi$ square inches. Length $=\dfrac{8\pi}{0.01}=800\pi$ inches.

questions.question: On a sheet of graph paper, Leo draws the line segment from $(0,6)$ to $(3,0)$. Through how many unit squares of the grid does the segment pass?
questions.solution: A segment between opposite corners of an $a\times b$ grid passes through $a+b-\gcd(a,b)$ squares: $3+6-\gcd(3,6)=3+6-3=6$.

questions.question: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius $5$. What is the area of the square?
questions.solution: The diagonal of the square equals the diameter $10$, so the side is $\frac{10}{\sqrt2}$ and the area is $\frac{100}{2}=50$.

questions.question: A small van has $2$ rows with $3$ seats each. Three passengers choose seats at random. What is the probability that all three sit in the front row?
questions.solution: There are $\binom{6}{3}=20$ equally likely sets of seats, and only $\binom{3}{3}=1$ puts all three in front: $\frac{1}{20}$.
